name: Osteopetrosis and Related Disorders

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Radiological Diagnostic Criteria for Osteopetrosis

criteria.description: Diffuse increased bone density and sclerosis on radiographs
Evidence of bone marrow failure including anemia, thrombocytopenia, or leukopenia
Identification of pathogenic variants in osteoclast-related genes (e.g., CLCN7, TCIRG1)
Presence of characteristic clinical features such as cranial nerve compression or pathological fractures

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Diffuse radiologic bone sclerosis plus either bone marrow failure or genetic confirmation
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing is recommended to confirm subtype and guide management.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Diffuse osteosclerosis with 'bone within bone' appearance
Cranial nerve compression leading to vision or hearing loss
searchTerms: nerve pressure causing vision or hearing loss
loss of sight or hearing from nerve damage

common.symptomName: Anemia due to bone marrow failure
searchTerms: low blood counts due to marrow
enlarged liver and spleen from blood cell production
big liver and spleen from blood disorders

common.symptomName: Delayed tooth eruption and dental abnormalities
searchTerms: dental abnormalities with slow tooth development

occasional.symptomName: Hydrocephalus due to skull base sclerosis
searchTerms: pressure in head due to skull bone hardening

occasional.symptomName: Increased susceptibility to infections due to marrow failure
searchTerms: frequent infections from low blood cells
weak immune system due to bone marrow failure
infections caused by poor blood cell production
drooping on one side of face
low blood calcium causing muscle cramps
tingling and twitching due to low calcium

laboratory: Pancytopenia due to bone marrow failure
imaging: Diffuse increased bone density on X-ray
Skull base sclerosis with foraminal narrowing
genetic: Mutations in CLCN7, TCIRG1, OSTM1, and other osteoclast-related genes
other: Bone biopsy showing defective osteoclast resorption activity

distinguishingFeatures: Normal or decreased bone density compared to osteopetrosis
Defective bone mineralization rather than increased density

redFlags: Rapid onset of bone marrow failure symptoms
Cranial nerve deficits indicating nerve compression
Recurrent pathological fractures with minimal trauma
references: Stark Z, Savarirayan R. Osteopetrosis. Orphanet J Rare Dis. 2009;4:5.
Sobacchi C, et al. Osteopetrosis: genetics, treatment and new insights into osteoclast function. Nat Rev Endocrinol. 2013;9(9):522-536.
